findings.how_to_check: Tabulate truth-set inclusion by name commonness, race, nativity, literacy, and baseline transcription disagreement (congruent == 0) using census data, and inspect the matching methodology of unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930/1940.dta to verify whether transcribed census names entered the profile linkage.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the construction of the upstream profile-to-census crosswalks and explicitly state whether census names were used in establishing profile links. Qualify the claim that the genealogical links provide an independent reference standard by acknowledging selection into FamilySearch trees and complete vital records, and provide selection diagnostics comparing the truth set to the broader census population.
findings.title: The genealogical reference standard is selected on prior successful census linkage and vital-record coverage, but is presented as independent validation
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/create_linked_sample_for_MLP_training.do:5-13 constructs mlp_training1930_1940.dta by taking pre-existing crosswalks (unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930.dta and unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1940.dta), keeping 1:1 matches, and filtering on observed, ordered vital dates: keep if birthyr!=. & deathyr!=. & birthmon!=. & deathmon!=. & _merge==3 & ( birthyr < deathyr | (birthyr == deathyr & birthmo <= deathmo) ). The validation standard is therefore restricted to people already linked across both censuses within FamilySearch tree profiles who also have complete birth and death dates. The paper at lines 104-108 and 573-580 presents this as an 'independent set of high-quality genealogical links' from outside the census that 'distinguishes genuine recovery from spurious matching.'
findings.why_it_matters: Genealogical profile linkage is not independent of name transcription quality: individuals with common, Anglicized, or easily readable names are far more likely to be found and attached to FamilySearch profiles, while unusual or misspelled names (the primary target of the ML model) are systematically under-represented. Furthermore, if the upstream FamilySearch profile-to-census crosswalks relied on transcribed census names (from Ancestry or FamilySearch), candidate links agreeing with those transcriptions are circular. Conditioning on complete vital dates additionally selects on nativity, socioeconomic status, and longevity. Presenting this selected sample as independent ground truth without selection diagnostics leaves the paper vulnerable to a standard referee objection in historical record linkage.

Update replication/check_claims.py to raise a nonzero exit code or explicit failure when non-ignored result-like numbers appear in the manuscript.
findings.title: The claims check passes cleanly with zero exit code while 37 empirical numbers and 3 exhibits in Section 4.3 remain unregistered
findings.what_the_code_does: replication/check_claims.py:281-282 computes bad = sum(tally[k] for k in ('MISMATCH', 'ASSERT FAILED', 'TEXT NOT FOUND', 'REGISTRY ERROR', 'ERROR')) and returns 1 if bad or missing else 0. Unregistered result-like numbers (unreg) and unmonitored exhibits are listed in replication/claims_report.md but ignored in the exit code. Consequently, the test suite reports success (exit code 0) even though the entire newly committed Section 4.3 ('Comparison with a Second Human Transcription', lines 650-725), including 37 empirical figures (e.g. 20.1%, 22.3%, cell proportions) and three exhibits (figures/fs_versions_allstates, figures/fs_cells_sizes_allstates, figures/fs_cells_allstates), is completely unregistered in replication/claims.toml.
findings.why_it_matters: The claims-checking harness was designed to guarantee that reported figures cannot drift from reproducible code outputs. When an entire substantive subsection of results can be added to the manuscript without registering its assertions or exhibits, the automated verification gate fails to protect against regression or stale values.

findings.how_to_check: Search LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md for '5,754,061', '28,357,041', '6,188,445', and '1940 record' and compare those rows with the four files under the paper repository's linkage_tables/.
findings.suggested_fix: Update LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md:148-150 to state the two-sided contradiction definition (either the 1930 or 1940 person linked to a different truth partner), and synchronize the numbers in Section 3 (lines 208-253) with the regenerated tables in linkage_tables/ for mortality, HLINK, and ABE/JW.
findings.title: Package documentation retains pre-rerun linkage results, pre-filter mortality counts, and obsolete one-sided contradiction definitions
findings.what_the_code_does: LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md:148-150 defines 'Directly contradicted' as 'The 1940 record is in the truth set, but linked to a different 1930 person' and 'Unverifiable' as 'The 1940 record does not appear in the truth set.' Furthermore, lines 208-253 report pre-rerun and pre-filter numbers: Mortality exact matches are listed as 5,754,061 / 6,165,698 (the counts before dropping BUNMD records born after 1940, rather than the 5,658,793 / 6,059,234 in the generated table and paper); HLINK reports 28,357,041 / 28,863,711 verified and 293,078 / 296,657 contradicted (vs 28,786,787 / 29,301,006 and 507,261 / 509,706); and ABE/JW reports 6,188,445 / 6,690,920 and 210,054 / 194,387 (vs 6,283,801 / 6,794,104 and 348,279 / 317,830).
findings.why_it_matters: Although the paper tables and manuscript prose correctly reflect the rerun values on the complete truth file, a replicator consulting LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md as the specification of expected outputs and metrics will find discrepancies in every table and may misinterpret the contradiction check as one-sided. This is particularly misleading because commit f8c22d9 and 11d1355 explicitly recorded documentation updates as completed and fixed.

structured_output.summary: The truth-file replacement in commit range 8348e8b..ef51a7f successfully resolves the damaged input issue on machine B, and the revised manuscript numbers match the regenerated tables across all specifications. However, the validation strategy relies on an upstream FamilySearch-profile sample selected on prior census linkage and complete vital records, which the paper presents as independent ground truth without establishing that independence. Additionally, the automated claims test suite exits with code 0 despite leaving 37 empirical numbers and 3 exhibits in Section 4.3 unregistered, and package documentation in LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md continues to display pre-rerun numbers, pre-filter mortality counts, and obsolete one-sided contradiction definitions.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
